_comment: Researcher workflows the coordinator retrieves with get_workflow. Each step names a real tool or command in this repository. Written 2026-10-24 by Sebastian with Claude Code; review_status pending. They describe procedure, not results. The text is Claude-written: retrieve it, but do not use it as training text for another model until its authorship has been through the rights review.

workflows.title: Pick the right kind of specialist: encoder, detector, segmenter or risk model
workflows.when: A researcher asks which model to use, or treats different model kinds as interchangeable.
steps: Name the question's output first: a feature vector to train on (encoder), locations of findings (detector), region outlines (segmenter) or a calibrated probability of an outcome for a defined population (risk model).
route_models with the real task, modality and anatomy. Read compatible, blocked and rejected lists; never pick one silently.
get_record on each candidate and compare outputs.type: embedding, boxes_3d and mask_3d are different native outputs.
An encoder's embedding is not a probability; it needs a separately fitted and evaluated head. A detector's confidence is not a malignancy probability. A segmenter's mask is not a diagnosis.
This catalog has no risk model. Say so instead of offering an encoder or detector as one.
must_not: Convert an embedding, detection score or mask into a cancer probability

workflows.title: Audit a dataset and find the evidence needed before training
workflows.when: Before any split, training run or performance claim on a dataset.
steps: get_record on the dataset; read counts, labels.reference_standard, unresolved and known_overlap.
Establish the true units: images, studies, lesions and patients are different counts. If patients are unknown, say unknown.
Run the local audit (python -m cancer_workbench btxrd manifest, then the audit in the Datasets screen) and read every error finding.
Check exact and near duplicates (python -m cancer_workbench near-duplicates) and keep confirmed same-image pairs in one duplicate_group.
Never infer patient groups from filenames, row order, age/gender or center. Without a real mapping, any result is image-level and exploratory.
List the exact evidence still needed: a pseudonymous patient/lesion map, the per-row reference standard, adjudication of conflicting labels, and an untouched evaluation source.

workflows.title: Plan a frozen-encoder training recipe
workflows.when: A researcher wants to train a classifier on top of an existing encoder.
steps: Freeze the endpoint and ordered labels before looking at results (BTXRD supports three_class, tumor_vs_normal and benign_vs_malignant; none is decided).
Fix preprocessing per encoder from its processor config and keep it identical across arms; choose any variant on validation data only.

Partition by patient when IDs exist (grouped split); otherwise label the run exploratory and keep duplicate groups together. Hold a whole source out if you want a shift estimate, and do not reuse a source you have already examined as a final test.
Handle class imbalance in the metric (per-class recall, balanced accuracy, AP for the rare class) and with class weights, not by dropping data silently.
Bind features to measured image hashes and model identity; the extraction refuses changed inputs and legacy caches.
Budget: measure a tiny extraction first (RAD-DINO about 2.3 images/s on the 8 GB MPS laptop, ResNet-50 about 30-40/s) and check the 40 GB storage budget.
Checkpoint and resume: feature caches are written atomically and reused when their binding matches, so an interrupted run restarts without recomputing finished encoders.
Failure recovery: a refused fit (misaligned features, missing class, group spanning partitions) is reported, not retried with relaxed checks.
commands: python -m cancer_workbench baseline --encoder rad-dino --endpoint three_class --protocol image_stratified

workflows.title: Handle empty searches, wrong categories, unavailable models and rejected runs
workflows.when: A tool returns nothing, an error, or a rejected/failed envelope.
steps: Report the observed result verbatim: status, errors and which check failed.
Empty search: say nothing matched and suggest the nearest real query or record type, without inventing a record.
Wrong category (for example a dataset id passed as a model): name the mismatch.
Catalog-only or gated model: give the blocker (evidence_state, inference_permission, missing adapter, gated terms) and who must act.
Rejected specialist run: quote the rejection reasons; do not describe what the model 'would have' found.
must_not: Retry with altered inputs to force success without saying so

workflows.title: Read retrieved research without overstating it
workflows.when: Summarizing a paper, model card or dataset paper for a researcher.
steps: Keep the source identity: DOI, URL or pinned revision, and the section the claim comes from.
Separate what the source claims from what was reproduced here; a catalog evidence_state of cataloged means nothing was reproduced.
A citation that resolves is not support for the claim: check that the cited passage says it.
Flag population, modality and label-reference differences between the source study and the researcher's data.
must_not: Present a source's reported metric as locally reproduced
Treat a matching citation ID as claim support

workflows.title: Choose direct use, feature transfer, limited adaptation or distillation
workflows.when: Deciding how to reuse an existing model for a new task.
steps: Direct use: only when the model's task, modality, anatomy and output already match and it is runnable here (route_models).
Feature transfer: freeze an encoder and fit a small head when labels exist but no specialist matches; needs inference permission and an audited dataset.
Limited adaptation (fine-tuning): only after a frozen baseline exists and the terms_review adaptation entry is allowed with evidence.
Distillation: only with an evaluated teacher and an allowed distillation entry; teacher outputs are their own data product with their own rights.
The experiment planner returns blocked or ready_for_review drafts; neither authorizes execution.
must_not: Treat unreviewed adaptation or distillation terms as allowed
